evidence: Self-documented instrumentation artifact with a coherent, appropriately-scoped mechanism. The 1.2.1 wheel ran AIC timing predictions as per-request Python callbacks whose wall-time leaked into the simulated clock; the 1.3.0 source build runs the same predictions in-core (Rust) in microseconds (twopool sec. and apendice env table). Because a per-request hook slower than the events it prices adds variable wall-time, the inflation concentrates in the extreme tail (max), which is exactly the scoped claim ('extreme tail maxima only'). This is why wheel-based runs were retained only for cheap coverage sweeps while all headline/load-sweep runs use the source build. Caveat: the 'only' (max inflated but p99/p50 unaffected) is a before/after observation from their own runs; the provenance DB v_pool_latency carries max_ms as null for these rows, so the exact quantile-selectivity is not independently re-derivable here. Mechanism is sound and the claim is presented as a guard, appropriately hedged.
fix: If challenged, cite the specific wheel-vs-source run pair showing p99 unchanged while max inflated, to substantiate 'maxima only'.
